system_scope.summary: The system is an Event framework intended to be used by an application, in which application logic and the framework are highly inter-dependent. It comprises a Main module that is part of the framework, an Event Manager that interacts directly with application handlers, an Event Queue, and a base Handler component extended by standard and application-specific handlers. The business goal is to provide this framework so applications can handle and process events through component interaction and utilize the framework's services.

business_drivers.statement: Provide an Event framework to be used by an application.
Handle and process events through component interaction.
Allow application components to utilize the framework services.
The system must handle system termination via a STOP handler.
The system must maintain itself in an idle state until input is received.
Variability is named as an architectural driver for this system.
Reliability is named as an architectural driver for this system.
Conceptual Integrity is named as an architectural driver for this system.
Functionality is named as an architectural driver for this system.
Modifiability is named as an architectural driver for this system.

architecture_evidence.statement: The architecture documentation status is 'fully developed architecture with class diagrams, component descriptions, and defined component interactions.'
The application logic and the framework are described as highly inter-dependent.
The Main module is part of the framework.
The Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers.
The architecture features an Event Queue component.
The architecture has a base Handler component that is extended by standard handlers and application-specific handlers.
The system accepts input via a Command Line Interface (CLI).
Single processor execution is implied, i.e. sequential event processing.
Events must be dispatched in a First-Come-First-Served (FIFO) pattern.
The system must maintain an 'idle wait' state until input is received.
Application logic is embedded within framework components.
The performance proxy used for this architecture is the number of components involved in a transaction.
Transaction speed is characterized qualitatively as slow, attributed to a high number of components involved.
The architecture limit for event managers is 1.
The architecture limit for event queues is 1.
The style probe target style for this evaluation is Event-Driven Architecture.
Style probe question posed against the target style: 'Does the system allow unauthorized access?'
Style probe question posed against the target style: 'Does the architecture portray data confidentiality?'
Style probe question posed against the target style: 'Does the architecture process any task in the fastest possible speed?'

open_questions.question: Can the components of the architecture be reused for future projects?
Can the framework be expanded in the future to accommodate a new application or new components?
Will the system handle any input given by the user and handle invalid input?
Is the architecture consistent in behavior?
Can any new application-specific functionality be added to the architecture?
Can the system be modified in a short time and cost-effective manner?
Does the architecture perform its event-processing task properly?

evidence: Present: a system description naming the framework's components (Main module, Event Manager, Event Queue, base Handler) and their coupling (evaluation_inputs.system_description).
Present: a hardware view stating CLI input and an implied single-processor, sequential execution model (evaluation_inputs.phase_2_architectural_context.hardware_view_description).
Present: documentation status recorded as fully developed with class diagrams and component interactions (evaluation_inputs.phase_1_discovery.initial_documentation_status).
Absent: no stakeholder roles, organization, or deployment environment beyond CLI/single-processor are supplied, so the operational context is only partially established.

Present: three business goals, two technical constraints, and five named architectural drivers (Variability, Reliability, Conceptual Integrity, Functionality, Modifiability) are listed in evaluation_inputs.business_context.
Absent: no priority ranking, relative importance, or stakeholder attribution is supplied for any business goal, constraint, or driver.
Present: component, connector, deployment, runtime-constraint, quantitative-parameter, and style-probe facts are all represented in the inputs (AE-1 through AE-19).
Absent: no numeric performance benchmark or workload is supplied, only a qualitative 'slow' characterization and a component-count proxy (evaluation_inputs.quantitative_model_parameters).

Absent: no description of security mechanisms (authentication, authorization, encryption) or failure/recovery behavior is supplied, despite style-probe questions and candidate scenarios raising these concerns.

gaps.description: No stakeholder priority or importance ranking is supplied for the business goals, technical constraints, or the five named architectural drivers (Variability, Reliability, Conceptual Integrity, Functionality, Modifiability), so their relative importance cannot be determined.
gaps.missing_evidence: A stakeholder-stated ranking or importance/difficulty rating for the business goals, constraints, or architectural drivers.
gaps.resolution_question: Which business goals, constraints, or architectural drivers take priority over the others, and according to which stakeholder?

gaps.description: The supplied material gives only a qualitative performance characterization ('slow due to high number of components involved') and a component-count proxy metric; no numeric response-time target, benchmark result, or workload volume is supplied.
gaps.missing_evidence: A numeric performance target, benchmark measurement, or workload/transaction-volume figure for event processing.
gaps.resolution_question: What quantitative response-time target or workload benchmark applies to event transaction processing?

gaps.description: The inputs pose style-probe questions about unauthorized access and data confidentiality (AE-17, AE-18), but no security mechanism (authentication, authorization, encryption, or data-protection design) is described anywhere in the supplied material.
gaps.missing_evidence: A description of any access-control, authentication, authorization, or encryption mechanism in the architecture.
gaps.resolution_question: Does the architecture include any security mechanism, and if so, what is it?

gaps.description: The raw candidate scenarios raise a concern about recovery after failure (RS-3), but no fault-detection, failover, or recovery mechanism is described in the supplied material.
gaps.missing_evidence: A description of fault detection, failover, or recovery behavior for the Event Manager, Event Queue, or handlers.
gaps.resolution_question: What recovery or fault-handling behavior, if any, does the architecture define for failures during event processing?

gaps.description: Beyond CLI input and an implied single-processor, sequential execution model, no deployment topology, network configuration, or distributed/multi-node execution detail is supplied, even though a candidate scenario (RS-10) raises execution in different environments.
gaps.missing_evidence: A deployment diagram or description of runtime nodes, network configuration, or distributed execution.
gaps.resolution_question: Does the system run on a single machine only, or is distributed or multi-environment deployment anticipated?
